samples.text: Explain chlor-alkali process and write balanced chemical equations for the reactions that occur. Name the gases obtained at the anode and cathode respectively. Mention two uses each of the two gases obtained in the above process.
samples.answer:
• Chlor-alkali process: When electricity is passed through an aqueous solution of sodium chloride (brine), it decomposes to form sodium hydroxide, chlorine and hydrogen.
• 2NaCl(aq) + 2H2O(l) → 2NaOH + Cl2 + H2
• Anode: Chlorine gas (Cl2); Cathode: Hydrogen gas (H2)
• Cl2 uses: (1) used in the preparation of bleaching powder. (2) to make drinking water free from germs.
• H2 uses: (1) used in the manufacture of ammonia/fertilisers. (2) used in fuels and margarine.
samples.explanation:
• Chlor-alkali process: passing electricity through an aqueous solution of sodium chloride (brine) decomposes it to give sodium hydroxide, chlorine and hydrogen.
• 2NaCl(aq) + 2H2O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + Cl2(g) + H2(g)
• Anode: Chlorine gas (Cl2) is liberated; Cathode: Hydrogen gas (H2) is liberated, while NaOH forms near the cathode.
• Uses of Cl2: (1) used to prepare bleaching powder; (2) used to make drinking water free from germs.
• Uses of H2: (1) used in the manufacture of ammonia for fertilisers; (2) used in fuels and in hydrogenating oils to make margarine.

samples.text:
(i) Carbon cannot form C4+ cation and C4– anion. Explain.
(ii) Define homologous series of carbon compounds. Why are the melting and boiling points of C4H10 higher than C3H8 or C2H6 ?
(iii) What happens when ethanol is heated with acidified potassium dichromate ?
samples.answer:
(i)
    • Carbon cannot form C4+ cation because removal of four electrons is energetically not possible. Carbon cannot form C4− anion because nucleus with six protons cannot hold ten electrons.
(ii)
    • A series of compounds in which the same functional group substitutes for hydrogen in carbon chain is called a homologous series.
    • Because of higher molecular mass of C4H10 than C3H8 or C2H6.
(iii)
    • Ethanoic acid / acetic acid / CH3COOH is formed /
    • CH3-CH2OH --[acidified K2Cr2O7 + Heat]--> CH3COOH
samples.explanation:
(i)
    • C⁴⁺: removing four electrons needs a very large amount of energy.
    • C⁴⁻: a nucleus with six protons cannot hold ten electrons. Hence carbon forms covalent bonds by sharing electrons.
(ii)
    • Homologous series: compounds with the same functional group whose successive members differ by a –CH₂ unit (14 u).
    • Melting and boiling points rise with molecular mass, and C₄H₁₀ has a higher molecular mass than C₃H₈ or C₂H₆.
(iii)
    • Acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ oxidises ethanol to ethanoic acid: CH₃CH₂OH → CH₃COOH; the orange solution turns green.

samples.text:
What happens when
(i) potassium iodide solution is added to lead (II) nitrate solution ?
(ii) zinc is added to copper (II) chloride solution ?
(iii) hydrogen gas is passed over hot copper (II) oxide ?

samples.answer:
(i)
    • Yellow precipitate of potassium iodide is formed.
    • 2KI + Pb(NO3)2 → PbI2 + 2KNO3
(ii)
    • Zinc will displace copper from copper chloride.
    • Zn + CuCl2 → ZnCl2 + Cu

    • The black coating of copper oxide will turn brown.
    • CuO + H2 → Cu + H2O
(Note: Award full marks if balanced chemical equation is written)

    • Zn + CuCl₂ → ZnCl₂ + Cu

    • Redox: CuO is reduced; black turns brown.

samples.text: What is a chemical reaction ? Describe one activity each to show that a chemical change has occurred in which (i) change of colour, and (ii) change in temperature has taken place.
samples.answer:
• A chemical reaction involves the breaking and making of bonds between atoms to produce new substances (reactants change into products).
(i)
    • Colour change: add lead nitrate solution to potassium iodide solution in a test tube — the colourless solution changes to a yellow precipitate.
    • Pb(NO3)2 + 2KI → PbI2↓ (yellow) + 2KNO3 (or any other example)
(ii)
    • Temperature change: calcium oxide reacts vigorously with water to produce slaked lime (calcium hydroxide), releasing a large amount of heat.
    • CaO(s) + H2O(l) → Ca(OH)2(aq) + Heat (or any other example)
samples.explanation:
• A chemical reaction is a process in which bonds between atoms break and new bonds form, converting reactants into new products, often with a visible sign such as colour or temperature change.
(i)
    • Colour change: lead nitrate solution mixed with potassium iodide solution turns from colourless to a yellow precipitate.
    • Pb(NO3)2 + 2KI → PbI2↓ (yellow) + 2KNO3.
(ii)
    • Temperature change: calcium oxide reacting with water is a highly exothermic activity.
    • CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2 + Heat, releasing a large amount of heat and forming slaked lime as the product.

samples.text:
(i) Leaves of chhui-mui plant begin to fold up and droop in response to a stimulus. Name the stimulus and write the cause for such a rapid movement. Is there any growth involved in the movement ?
(ii) Define geotropism in plants. What is meant by positive and negative geotropism ? Give one example of each type.
samples.answer:
(i)
    • Stimulus: touch.
    • Cause: the shape of the leaves changes due to a change in the amount of water in their cells.
    • No, growth is not involved in this movement.
(ii)
    • Geotropism: growth of a plant part in response to the pull of gravity.
    • Positive geotropism: movement of a plant part towards gravity, e.g., roots growing downwards.
    • Negative geotropism: movement of a plant part away from gravity, e.g., shoots growing upwards.
samples.explanation:
(i)
    • Stimulus: touch (a mechanical stimulus applied to the leaflets).
    • Cause: a rapid change in the water content (turgor pressure) of cells at the base of the leaflets, not any growth process.
    • No growth is involved — it is a quick, reversible turgor movement that occurs within seconds.
(ii)
    • Geotropism is the growth movement of a plant part in response to the pull of gravity.
    • Positive geotropism: movement of a plant part towards gravity — e.g., roots grow downwards into the soil.
    • Negative geotropism: movement of a plant part away from gravity — e.g., shoots grow upwards against gravity.

samples.text:
(a) Name a device which is used to :
    (i) Maintain a constant potential difference in a circuit.
    (ii) Change the electric current in an electric circuit.
(b) When the potential difference between the terminals of an electric heater is 110 V, a current of 5 A flows through it. What will be the value of current flowing through it when the potential difference is increased to 220 V ?
samples.answer:
(a)
    (i)
        • Battery / Electric cell
    (ii)
        • Rheostat / Variable resistance
(b)
    Resistance of the heater, R = V/I
    R = 110/5
    R = 22 Ω
    Current through the heater, I′ = V′/R
    = 220/22
    = 10 A
    /
    Alternate answer for (b):
    • According to Ohm’s law, potential difference is directly proportional to current.
    • When the potential difference is doubled, current will also be doubled. So, value of current will be 10A.
samples.explanation:
(a)
    • (i) Battery / cell maintains a constant potential difference.
    • (ii) Rheostat (variable resistance) changes the current.
(b)
    Given: V = 110 V, I = 5 A, V′ = 220 V
    R = V/I
    R = 110/5
    R = 22 Ω
    I′ = V′/R
    I′ = 220/22
    I′ = 10 A
    ∴ Doubling the voltage doubles the current to 10 A (resistance unchanged).

samples.text:
(i) How many bulbs of resistance 8 Ω each should be connected in parallel combination to draw a current of 2 A from a battery of 4 V ?
(ii) Name the device used for measuring electric current. How is it connected in a circuit ?
(iii) State Joule’s law of heating.
samples.answer:
(i)
    V= 4V, I= 2A
    Resistance of circuit R = V/I
    R = 4/2
    R = 2Ω
    Let ‘n’ be the number of bulbs
    1/R = 1/8 + 1/8 + 1/8 + 1/8 + ---n
    1/R = n/8
    1/2 = n/8
    n = 4
    Therefore, 4 bulbs of resistance 8 Ω should be connected in parallel.
(ii)
    • Ammeter
    • In series
(iii)
    • Heat generated through a current carrying conductor is directly proportional to square of current, resistance of conductor and time for which current flows in conductor. / H = I²Rt
samples.explanation:
(i)
    Given: V = 4 V, I = 2 A, each bulb = 8 Ω
    R = V/I
    R = 4/2
    R = 2 Ω
    1/R = n/8
    1/2 = n/8
    n = 4
    ∴ 4 bulbs must be connected in parallel.
(ii)
    • Ammeter, connected in series so the whole current passes through it.
(iii)
    • Heat produced in a conductor is directly proportional to the square of current, its resistance and the time of flow: H = I²Rt.

samples.text: "Proteins control the expression of various characters." Explain this statement by taking an example of "tallness" as a characteristic in plants.

samples.text:
(a) What are chromosomes ?
(b) Explain in brief how stability of DNA content of a species is ensured in sexually reproducing organisms ?
samples.answer:
(a)
    • Chromosomes carry genes which control the traits of an organism/chromosomes contain information for inheritance of features from parents to next generation in the form of DNA (Deoxy ribonucleic acid) molecule.
(b)
    • Each cell has two copies of each chromosome, one from male and the other from female parents, which get halved during the formation of germ cells/gametes.
    • After fusion of the germ cells a zygote is formed which restores the normal number of chromosomes and the same amount of DNA in the progeny.
samples.explanation:
(a)
    • Chromosomes are thread-like structures in the cell nucleus that carry genes controlling an organism's traits, in the form of DNA.
(b)
    • Each cell has two copies of every chromosome; gamete formation halves this number.
    • Fusion of two gametes at fertilisation restores the normal chromosome number and DNA content in the zygote, keeping it stable across generations.

samples.text:
(i) State the role of rings of cartilage present in the throat.
(ii) Discuss the role of the ribs and diaphragm when air is taken in during the breathing cycle.
(iii) Why do we get muscle cramps during heavy exercise ? Explain.
samples.answer:
(i)
    • 'Rings of cartilage' ensure that the air passage does not collapse in the absence of air.
(ii)
    • Ribs are lifted → diaphragm flattens → chest cavity becomes larger → air is sucked into the lungs (alveoli) and we breathe in.
(iii)
    • Due to lack of oxygen in muscle cells (anaerobic respiration), pyruvate is converted into lactic acid; build-up of lactic acid in muscles causes cramps.
samples.explanation:
(i)
    • Rings of cartilage in the throat (trachea) keep the air passage from collapsing even when there's little air inside, ensuring a continuous, open pathway for airflow.
(ii)
    • During inhalation: the ribs move up and outward while the diaphragm contracts and flattens, together enlarging the chest cavity; this reduces internal pressure, drawing air into the lungs.
(iii)
    • During heavy exercise, muscle cells don't get enough oxygen and switch to anaerobic respiration, converting pyruvate into lactic acid instead of carbon dioxide; the resulting build-up of lactic acid in the muscles causes painful cramps.

samples.text:

samples.text: What is scattering of light ? How is scattering of light different from reflection of light ? Explain.
samples.answer:
• The phenomenon of spreading light in different directions on interaction with particles of the medium.
• Light bounces back in a fixed direction after reflection while in scattering of light, it spreads in different directions. / Reflection of light is independent of the size of reflecting particles whereas the colour of the scattered light depends upon the size of scattering particles.
samples.explanation:
• Scattering: when light strikes tiny particles of a medium, it spreads out in different directions.
• Difference:
    • Reflection sends light back in one fixed direction; scattering spreads it in all directions.
    • Reflection does not depend on particle size, whereas the colour of scattered light depends on the size of the scattering particles (e.g. blue sky).
